title: UnitCon: Synthesizing Targeted Unit Tests for Java Runtime Exceptions
datasets: RQ1: 198 targeted Java runtime-exception cases from Bears (14), Genesis (16), NPEX (59), VFix (29), and Defects4J (80); each benchmark case has a target runtime exception.
RQ2: 51 current open-source Java repositories for Infer NPE alarm inspection; 4,290 alarms, UnitCon generated crashes for 256, manually reviewed 26 and identified 21 unique bugs.
task: Targeted unit-test synthesis for runtime exceptions at a specified source location using static analysis; support crash reproduction and static-analysis alarm validation. Not LLM test generation and not a general functional-bug oracle.
input_setting: Given program and target exception location, Infer derives error conditions and method summaries; enumerative Java-like DSL constructs public API-call sequences, prioritizes using sufficient error conditions and prunes semantically redundant paths, then executes candidates to trigger the exception.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper Data Availability cites author Zenodo and UnitCon website. GitHub README states it is the paper artifact; FSE author page lists same authors/title; bundled paper.pdf matches title/author/DOI. GitHub repository HEAD pinned at f7ab2e23a57e12060b50af91cf7098dfc347b9ff.
source_commit_or_archive: prosyslab/unitcon-artifact commit f7ab2e23a57e12060b50af91cf7098dfc347b9ff; nested UnitCon submodule pinned in tree at 642930a. Zenodo v6 15460355 publishes 2.7GB implementation, 7.5GB Maven cache and 9.9GB result archive.
license: GitHub BSD-3-Clause LICENSE (paper itself CC BY 4.0); paper code license is explicit and accessible.
exact_models: No LLM/model used. Static analyzer: Facebook Infer/Pulse; baselines EvoSuite 1.2, UTBot 2024.6.3-228072f, Randoop 4.3.2, EvoFuzz, NPETest.
weights_status: Not applicable; no learned model or weights.
evaluation_route: Paper full text 22 pages, 12,516 words, SHA-256 recorded; GitHub README/License/Requirements/Status inspected and saved with hashes. Artifact has benchmark projects, scripts, Dockerfiles, UnitCon submodule, test outputs/expected exception metadata, and Zenodo archives. README reports 512GB RAM, Intel Xeon 2.90GHz, 188GB storage; full RQ1 takes 125 days sequentially or 33h UnitCon + 330h baselines in parallel, and an 8-project minimal RQ1 about 2 days. RQ3 reduced experiment 5 hours. RQ2 targeted bug reproduction is documented by Java-version-specific containers. No code execution.
blockers: Reproduction is compute/storage heavy: authors report 512GB RAM and 188GB storage; full experiment includes very long baselines.
Docker images/builds, Java 8/11/17/21 configurations, OCaml 4.13.1, Infer, Maven, and historical project dependencies create setup burden.
Paper has a precise public route and archived code/results; exact full-scale reproduction remains conditional on hardware, dependencies, and confirming target-case versions.
Task only targets runtime exceptions, with 80 Defects4J cases in its 198-case suite; RQ2 uses current project versions and Infer alarms. No BugsInPy or SWT-Bench and no LLM evaluation route.
concept_fit: High for causal triggering conditions: the method extracts path/error preconditions and uses object-state/method summaries to guide test construction; useful for root-cause conditions and targeted exception reproduction. It does not label broad bug-cause taxonomy and is not an LLM method.
recommendation: Strong supporting choice when the experiment needs targeted Defects4J runtime-exception tests and explicit sufficient error conditions. Source is publicly licensed and exact model is not needed, but full reproduction needs unusually large resources; first use the published 8-project minimal route or cached results for artifact assessment. Not a direct benchmark for concept-guided LLM generation.
